Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. No appears on behalf of the respondent informant despite service of notice.
3. In terms of the F.I.R. lodged as a missing person report, it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant.

Subsequently, in the statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the prosecution story rather she stated she had gone out of her own free will and knew the applicant for the last three years.
As per the F.I.R., the age of the victim has been mentioned as 15 years.

1 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that as per the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the tentative age of the victim is 18 years.

There is no definite document to conclusive form the age of the victim and the same shall be determined by the trial court at the time of the time in terms of the procedure prescribed under Section 94 of he Juvenile Justice Act.

The applicant is in jail since 8.10.2022 and has no criminal history, hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
5.
Learned A.G.A. also opposed the prayer for bail.

6. Considering the two statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. in favour of the applicant coupled with the fact that the age of the victim and the determination of the age of the victim shall be decided at the time of trial in terms of the procedure prescribed under Section 94 of he Juvenile Justice Act.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents and is in custody since 8.10.2022 and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
